title: Bodhapañcadaśikā — Fifteen Verses on Awakening
author: Abhinavagupta
text:
The Bodhapañcadaśikā is a verse-treatise of fifteen stanzas by Abhinavagupta, a compact exposition from the mature Trika literature of tenth-century Kashmir. Its subject is bodha — awakening or illumination — treated not as an achievement but as the unsetting light in which bright and dark alike are held. The verses move from the nature of that light to the one who dwells within it, and onward to the relation of consciousness, world, and the Lord who is neither a second thing nor a distant one.

Its juice: what never sets is not seen occasionally but is the condition of all seeing. The fifteen verses press a single recognition — the illuminator is never itself an object of illumination — until the reader is left standing, quite literally, in what was doing the looking.
